Fans of 2D souls-likes will certainly appreciate the stamina management and whiff-punishing. But the folks who will get the most out of MÖRK BORG HERESY SUPREME will be those familiar with the tabletop role-playing game it's based on. To those folks I say: [i]this is a terrific translation[/i]. Nihilism and futility are unapologetically front and center. Your team of sickly scum are doing well for themselves if they can survive more than 2 hits before being Broken. Combat demands timing and patience, and is aided by using each character classes' unique (and sometimes less obvious) advantages. Magic is dangerous and prone to backfiring, but one successful cast can save you just long enough to die in the next room. The truly resourceful can squeak out a meager victory by chucking random inventory items at goblins & the undead, even (as I once managed to do) fell a looming troll by desperately hurling coins. Your reward is always more punishment, and RNG is holding the whip. The tabletop game's grim artwork is present throughout, complete with iconic fonts & color palette. All of it sets the mood and tone succinctly; you will know precisely what you're in for once the brutal opening cinematic plays & the title screen growls at you in a single unbreaking drone. All in all, it recreates the feeling of a MÖRK BORG campaign so well that I caught myself role-playing in it. When one unusually lucky party managed to survive together long enough to see the 7th Psalm, and I knew they'd never make it to their next mission's destination in time, I sold all items in inventory, bought the lads a round of Grave Wine, and they watched the darkness swallow the darkness with their feet dangling off a bridge over the Mur, enjoying a bottle & a song. None of that stuff about "dangling feet off a bridge" was actually in the game, but the systems & mood made pretending it was possible, and I enjoy that. Then next time round, I rolled up an Esoteric Hermit, and his single HP was taken from him 3 rooms into the 1st area, after he lost an argument with a floating skull. All of that WAS in the game and I love how that happened too. Bottom line, if you're into methodical, unforgiving gameplay, MÖRK BORG HERESY SUPPEME will scratch that itch for sure. If you're into irreverent chaotic death metal art, or just a general aesthetic worship of entropy, it'll be a fun game for you to look at. And if you played the TTRPG, I'm amazed you're even still reading this & not furiously hammering the BUY button. It's really good now, and I think once all the content fills it in & the bugs are well & truly bashed, it'll be truly great.

Right now, in the state this game is in, I can’t recommend it for anyone - even with the “Early Access” aspect. There is potential here, but it is buried in a lot of technical issues. The game has a very inconsistent frame rate, in addition to freezing, stuttering, crashing and tearing constantly. I haven’t sworn this much at a game since Catherine on the highest difficulty mode. Not because the game is hard - but because it is so broken that it probably shouldn’t even be at the Early Access level yet. There is nothing worse dying because the game there is a frame rate lag between button pressing and the action on the screen. Or when you hold the Shield Button down and it turns itself off of its own accord. Or when you go through a randomly generated dungeon and finally get to the end of something, only to have the game crash on you and you lose all the progress. There is so much that needs to be fixed in this game that I would happily get a refund, and wait to see if things get better in the finished product, except I backed this on Kickstarter and so I am out of luck. But the good thing about an Early Access game is that there is nowhere to go but up. Trophies don’t pop, I’ve gotten the troll finger twice. No achievement. I’ve done three games in a row with a 1 HP character and the trophy for starting a run with a 1HP character has never popped. Besides the aforementioned issues with the game’s inability to run smoothly, is that it is so easy to lose your progress. “Continue” just lets you start back at the beginning of the dungeon, which would be fine with a game that runs properly. With the game in the state it is in, it is like herpes on the Pope’s ring. Saving between rooms until the game gets this corrected would make things a lot less annoying, but it would also make the game TOO easy in the final product. So after all that, let’s talk about what the game does correctly. First, the game oozes style. It looks like Mork Borg come to life, which is impressive as hell. The character designs are lifted straight from the tabletop books. The animation, while janky, actually fits the game’s look, but this seems to be a happy accident more than anything else. The look and feel of the world is great, and it makes me wish/hope the team does a turn based RPG, adventure game or a visual novel with the same ambience. The music is a lot of fun, as is the voice acting when there is some. I also like the opening cinematic. It’s a great intro to the world of Mork Borg of you’ve never played the TTRPG. I like the basic combat feel of the game. It’s like an old NES game in simplicity but difficulty. Enemies are easy to predict and get past, until the game gets wonky. Right now, due to the many bugs, it feels like a single character “Heroes of the Lance,” more than anything else, but I can see this being more like a Castlevania 3 experience. Right now, the biggest issue with combat is the slowdown or frame rate issues if you have more than two enemies generated in a battle. Two Gobins and three Dire Mosquitos? Your Steam Deck will hate you for this. This is going to cause you to get hit and thus die when you otherwise wouldn’t. Dying because of the game’s performance issues rather than your own slip ups is extremely annoying. Once the bugs get worked out, this should be a joy to play instead of a grueling slogfest. But currently it’s just so frustrating to finish a dungeon and lose all your progress because the game crashes, or when your character and the troll hunter end up on top of each other and you can’t turn around anymore to aim or block, so it’s just waiting to die. In the current state of the game, 0.3, I believe(?), the bad more than outweighs the good, but the devs are constantly tweaking the game (like three updates on the 25th of May alone!) and I really think over the coming months, they can right this ship. However the game’s Early Access state is going to turn away more people than it would had they just waited to release the finished product. A lot of people unfortunately play a game in EA, find it has issues, and don’t give it a second chance. Right now I am giving this a thumb’s down because it is pretty bad currently, and I’d rather warn you away by saying, “Wait for the final version than playing what is currently here.” Maybe I’m being too optimistic in thinking that real improvements are on the way, and if not, the the negative review will stand. Otherwise, I will be more than happy to change this to a thumb’s up once it is in a more playable state.

As with many people who have played MÖRK BORG Heresy Supreme, I backed the project on Kickstarter because I am a big fan of the MÖRK BORG TTRPG. As a fan of the TTRPG, I have to say that this game nails the feeling and vibe of the TTRPG, right down the stressful ability checks when interacting with objects and traps in the game world. I know a number of people on here have pointed out that game can be janky or have stability issues, but I feel lucky that I haven't encountered any real issues playing mostly on the Steam Deck. Does it have a few rough edges? Sure, but it is in very early access, so I feel that those are understandable. Having played the alpha demo earlier in the year, it's already come a long way since then and I can see a lot of potential. As far as gameplay goes, the combat is intentionally slower-paced to fit with the grungy and unheroic vibe of MÖRK BORG, and it delivers well on that, feeling visceral and oppressive. The game is already really fun if you enjoy the aesthetic, music, and side-scrolling rogue-lite dungeon crawling. Personally I recommend it, and I'm excited to see how much further things go.

An amazingly faithful adaptation to a TTRPG I've been playing for years. It seems like every step forward has given the game more depth and replayabliity without compromising on the unforgiving nature of Mörk Borg. The game could have easily been brutal for brutals sake and im glad its not. I of course have run into a couple bugs here and there too. A few simple achievements I should have gotten never showed up, and the game will crash just about every other time I minimize the screen for something. I understand how these are bigger issues for folks but they dont take me out of it really. The devs are really responsive to feedback and the game is only getting better for it. The difference in performance between this and the Beta alone is huge already. I'll start worrying about deeper performance issues if they persist past the full release. As for now, I'm just enjoying my time in the Dying World.

THIS GAME SHOULD NOT EXIST! BUT IT DOES! As a fan of Mork Borg, my eyes couldn't believe this when I first saw it: A side scrolling dungeon crawling action oriented hack and slash rpg, yet completely accurate to the rules, setting, art style, and vibe of the Mork Borg pen and paper roleplaying game. When I played it (enjoy the learning curve, it flows with more player experience), I personally had a great and flawless experience. The settings and creatures are right from the pages, and the only downside was I wanted ALL of the classes immediately, although Fanged Deserter may be most suited for pure combat. The fact that the randomization of Mork Borg extends to characters of the same class, both in looks and special abilities, not to mention quirks, ands a huge amount of variation already. Be sure to learn all of your buttons, movements, and omen/item usage or you won't last long. Don't get crowded, and use dodge and dash for defensive capabilities (Fanged Deserter shield is must use). This is a must buy for any fan of Mork Borg, even if you are terrible at it. It nails it all, right down to the Doomsday Clock.

I really want to like this game. I love the TTRPG and the setting and how it looks. But I can't recommend it. It's hard, but in the wrong way: It's not challenging, it's punishing. One mistake pretty much means you have to start all over again. And since there's (mostly) one main quest (with randomized elements), that means playing the first few segments of the game over and over and over and over and over and over... and it just takes. so. long. to. do. *anything* (looking at you, unskippable cut scenes). It really takes the fun out of it. Here's hoping the balancing gets reworked in the future.

The core experience is fun, unforgiving, and brimming with atmosphere. It is a great adaptation of the TTRPG, and this also means it is not for everyone; the devs actively encourage people to edit files and tune the experience to players' own preferences. This is a core aspect of the TTRPG as well, but it also means that more "casual" (to use an overused term) players may struggle. Be aware that at the time of review, it is still in very early access, so many aspects of the game are inaccessible and buggy. But good things come to those who wait, and as it stands this game has a lot of potential. I love games that are atmosphere first, and I don't mind dying over and over again, so be aware that this ain't comparable to a AAA experience. But it's metal, it's punk, and it's proper MÖRK BORG. Oh, and the soundtrack is actually, *properly* sludge and doom metal. Too often have I been promised a metal soundtrack and fell headfirst into the realm of fantasy choirs and power strings. Not this f*cking time.

A desperate attempt to endure the coming Apocalypse in a cursed, unjust dark fantasy world... Combat is brutal, choices are lethal, and survival is a temporary insult to fate... A flail to the face!
